quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: When must you slow down, yield, and prepare to stop for pedestrians?

options.text: Only when a traffic light is yellow or red.
When they are crossing or walking on the roadway.
Only when they are in marked crosswalks.
Only when they are crossing the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: When they are crossing or walking on the roadway.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians who are walking on or crossing the roadway. Do this even if they are not following the right-of-way rules.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: What can help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Quick stops waste time and fuel because you must accelerate again. Look ahead while driving. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: Which must you obey over the other three?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions come first. They have authority over all signs, signals, and road markings.

questions.question: When making a right turn, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Position your car as far to the right as possible before turning right. Do not cut across traffic lanes.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You can turn right at a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What should you do when another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually once the road ahead is clear. This lets the tailgater pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Move right if possible. If you cannot, slow down gradually when it is safe. Never brake suddenly as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, reduce speed, and pull over to a safe spot to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, reduce speed, and pull over to a safe spot to stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, steering is harder. Slow down and drive to a safe area off the road to stop.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the road shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without hard braking. Carefully steer back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely and easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely and easily.
questions.explanation: Slowing down gives the passing driver more space in front of your car. This helps them complete the pass faster and more safely.

questions.question: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street if:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle has the speed needed to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street if all three conditions are met: you can clearly see the road ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can pass safely. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: When parked facing downhill, your front wheels should be:

options.text: Turned toward the curb or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turned toward the curb or shoulder.
questions.explanation: When parked facing downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or shoulder. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: Which suggestion does NOT help you drive safely at night?

options.text: Know that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Do not look into oncoming headlights. Your eyes will adjust to the bright light, and then take time to readjust when the vehicle passes. During this recovery time, you cannot see well and are essentially driving blind.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Gets processed by your body more quickly.
Reduces the number of driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down your reactions.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more driving errors.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and go find help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road and signal other drivers.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you remain in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you remain in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You will be easier to find in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, look:
questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a road crossing ahead is coming.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a hill or curve because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving onto the highway shoulder.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not pass by driving onto the shoulder. Do not pass over a solid yellow line. All of these are illegal and dangerous.
